info.title: Data Collection Entries

businessRules.ruleTitle: The recordDateTime is the date time which the event is recorded in the system of record with an event.status.code=complete
creationDateTime is the date that the event is created.  If a System of Record creates the event instance then it sets the creationDateTime.

If request contains ADP-Act-As-OrgOID, ADP-Act-As-AssociateOID and ADP-Acting-SessionID header values, SOR MUST use ADP-Act-As-AssociateOID header value to authorize the data requested, NOT associateoid header value to authorize the data.
A complete event has /data/eventContext and /data/output
If the event is declared by an actor then the creationDateTime is the date time when the first call is made to the System of Record.
The only information that must be valued in the meta for the events header are the standard codelist references for priorityCode, eventStatusCode, and serviceCategoryCode
An event notification does not include the transform or meta objects.
/data/transform is only used during the recording of the event.  The transform is the data that is provided by a user/machine to complete the recording of the event.
An event notification includes the /data/eventContext and /data/output objects.
A self link is included in the /data/links with 1 links item with the following 2 properties: rel=”self” href=”/events-notifications/{domain}/v1/{event-name}/{eventID}”

/data/input is optional.  Input communicates data that is needed to complete recording the event instance.  An example is a benefits.enroll event.  The input communicates the benefitOfferings (the choices) that the user has to make which are communicated in the transform.
An event instance which is being “worked on” has an event.status.code=inprogress
effectiveDateTime is the date that the event is effective from a business perspective
/data/output communicates the result of the event instance.
'associateoid' in the uri pattern should match the 'associateoid' in the request header parameter
/data/output may be provided during the recording of the event showing the intermediary results.
For Act-As or On-Behalf-Of requests, header 'Cache-Control: no-store' MUST be set to indicate on server or on UI the response object SHOULD not be cached
If there is no effective date from a business perspective then the effective date should be set equal to the record date time.
An event which is being recorded includes the /data/eventContext and the /data/transform during the composition phase (i.e. recording of the event).

If request contains ADP-On-Behalf-Of-OrgOID, ADP-On-Behalf-Of-AssociateOID and ADP-Acting-SessionID header values, SOR MUST use ADP-On-Behalf-Of-AssociateOID header value to authorize the data requested, NOT associateoid header value to authorize the data.
event.id is generated once an event is recorded with a event.status.code=complete
/data/schemaContext communicates the keys and properties that relate the event instance to a concrete concept (e.g. associate).

An SOR may return an HTTP 503 when they are down for a scheduled maintenance or for an outage.If an SOR is planning a maintenance window then they should plan on having an end point available to return the 503 with a standard confirmMessage.  The confirmMessage will contain a message stating the date and timeframe that the maintenance window is for.The SOR should return the Retry-After response-header field with the Date and Time when they expect the system to be available.  E.g. §  Retry-After: Fri, 31 Dec 1999 23:59:59 GMT  This does not need to be handled dynamically.  They can set the time that their maintenance window ends.
An event instance which has been recorded has an event.status.code=complete
An event instance may be created by a System of record for a user to complete. This event instance will have a event.status.code=created
Meta returns the context rules for each data section
All envelope data is set by the System of Record (e.g. event.ID, creationDateTime, recordDateTime, event.status.code, etc…
